Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic forecast errors and derive correction rules.

## Example 1: Date 2025-05-16
- History: Price started at 64.39 and ended at 73.41 (about +14%)
- Sentiment: Started at 0.67, became more positive, ended at 0.00
- Model forecasts: Start around 70.59, gradually decline to ~70.28
- True outcomes: Start around 70.99, gradually decline to ~70.40

The model under-forecasts the decline slightly. The sentiment ended at 0.00 (neutral/negative), which could indicate some remaining downward pressure not fully captured.

Let me look at the differences more carefully:
- At day 1: Model 70.59 vs True 70.99 (under by 0.40)
- At day 10: Model 69.00 vs True 70.94 (under by 1.94)
- At day 20: Model 73.81 vs True 75.94 (under by 2.13)

The model seems to be too conservative, especially when sentiment is positive but prices are still ramping up.

## Example 2: Date 2025-01-06
- History: Prices climbed from 68.31 to 75.94 (+11.6%)
- Sentiment: Mostly positive (12 out of 18 days with sentiment > 0), ending at 0.67
- Model forecasts: Start at 73.77, gradually decline to ~73.36
- True outcomes: Start at 74.36, continue climbing to 82.95+

This is a significant divergence. The model predicts prices will decline from the current level, but they continue climbing.

- Day 20: Model 73.61 vs True 80.88 (under by 7.27)
